arxiv-2010-07898.title: Diagonal unitary and orthogonal symmetries blablabl in quantum theory
arxiv-2010-07898.creator: Satvik Singh, Ion Nechita
arxiv-2010-07898.description: A 2020 arXiv research paper by Satvik Singh, Ion Nechita. We analyze bipartite matrices and linear maps between matrix algebras, which are respectively, invariant and covariant, under the diagonal unitary and orthogonal groups’ actions. By presenting an expansive list of examples from the literature, which includes notable entries like the Diagonal Symmetric states and the Choi-type maps, we show that this class of matrices (and maps) encompasses a wide variety of scenarios, thereby unifying their study.

arxiv-2104-11640.title: The crossing number of the generalized Petersen graph
arxiv-2104-11640.creator: P
arxiv-2104-11640.description:
A 2021 arXiv research paper by P. Abstract
The crossing number of a graph
G
in a surface
\Sigma
, denoted by
cr_{\Sigma}(G)
, is the minimum number of pairwise intersections of edges in a drawing of
G
in
\Sigma

k
be an integer satisfying
k\geq 3

P(3k,k)
is the graph with vertex set
V(P(3k,k))=\{u_{i},v_{i}|i=1,2,\cdots,3k\}

arxiv-2107-00573.title: Extraction of Product and Higher Moment Weak Values: Applications in Quantum State Reconstruction and Entanglement Detection
arxiv-2107-00573.creator: Sahil, Sohail, Subhrajit Modak, Sibasish Ghosh, Arun Kumar Pati
arxiv-2107-00573.description: Abstract Weak measurements introduced by Aharonov, Albert and Vaidman (AAV) can provide informations about the system with minimal back action. Weak values of product observables (commuting) or higher moments of an observable are informationally important in the sense that they are useful to resolve some paradoxes, realize strange quantum effects, reconstruct density matrices, etc.

arxiv-2108-05843.title: Floquet theory of photoinduced topological phase transitions in the organic salt α \alpha -(BEDT-TTF) 2 I 3 irradiated with elliptically polarized light
arxiv-2108-05843.creator: Keisuke Kitayama, Yasuhiro Tanaka, Masao Ogata, Masahito Mochizuki
arxiv-2108-05843.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Keisuke Kitayama, Yasuhiro Tanaka, Masao Ogata, Masahito Mochizuki. We theoretically investigate possible photoinduced topological phase transitions in the organic salt α \alpha -(BEDT-TTF) 2 I 3 , which possesses a pair of inclined massless Dirac-cone bands between the conduction and valence bands under uniaxial pressure. The Floquet analyses of a driven tight-binding model for this material reveal rich photoinduced variations of band structures, Chern numbers, and Hall conductivities under irradiation with elliptically polarized light.

arxiv-2202-02292.title: 𝐙 ′ \mathbf{Z}^{\prime} -mediated Majorana dark matter: suppressed direct-detection rate and complementarity of LHC searches Preprint: LTH 1298, DESY-22-022
arxiv-2202-02292.creator: T. Alanne, F. Bishara, J. Fiaschi, O. Fischer, M. Gorbahn, and U. Moldanazarova
arxiv-2202-02292.description: Abstract We study the direct-detection rate for axial-vectorial dark matter scattering off nuclei in an SU ⁡ ( 2 ) × U ⁡ ( 1 ) \mathrm{SU}(2)\times\mathrm{U}(1) invariant effective theory and compare it against the LHC reach. Current constraints from direct detection experiments are already bounding the mediator mass to be well into the TeV range for WIMP-like scenarios.

arxiv-2204-10033.title: Characterizations of classes of countable Boolean inverse monoids
arxiv-2204-10033.creator: Mark V. Lawson, Philip Scott
arxiv-2204-10033.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Mark V. Lawson, Philip Scott. arxiv-2402-09615.title: API Pack: A Massive Multi-Programming Language Dataset for API Call Generation
arxiv-2402-09615.creator: Zhen Guo MIT EECS zguo0525@mit.edu, Adriana Meza Soria MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab adriana.meza.soria@ibm.com Wei SunIBM Research sunw@us.ibm.com Yikang Shen MIT-IBM Watson AI Lab yikang.shen@ibm.com Rameswar PandaMIT-IBM Watson AI Lab rpanda@ibm.com
arxiv-2402-09615.description: Abstract We introduce API Pack, a massive multi-programming language dataset containing over one million instruction-API calls for improving the API call generation capabilities of large language models. Our evaluation highlights three key findings: First, fine-tuning on API Pack enables open-source models to outperform GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 in generating code for entirely new API calls.

arxiv-2407-08877.title: Analyzing Speech Motor Movement using Surface Electromyography in Minimally Verbal Adults with Autism Spectrum Disorder
arxiv-2407-08877.creator: Wazeer Zulfikar ∗, Nishat Protyasha ∗, Camila Canales, Heli Patel, James Williamson, Laura Sarnie, Lisa Nowinski, Nataliya Kosmyna, Paige Townsend, Sophia Yuditskaya, Tanya Talkar, Utkarsh Oggy Sarawgi ∗ ∗ {}^{*}{{}^{*}}, Christopher McDougle, Thomas Quatieri, Pattie Maes, Maria Mody
arxiv-2407-08877.description: Abstract Adults who are minimally verbal with autism spectrum disorder (mvASD) have pronounced speech difficulties linked to impaired motor skills. Existing research and clinical assessments primarily use indirect methods such as standardized tests, video-based facial features, and handwriting tasks, which may not directly target speech-related motor skills.

arxiv-2504-00691.title: ToVE: Efficient Vision-Language Learning via Knowledge Transfer from Vision Experts
arxiv-2504-00691.creator: Yuanchen Wu, Junlong Du, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding, Xiaoqiang Li
arxiv-2504-00691.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Yuanchen Wu, Junlong Du, Ke Yan, Shouhong Ding, Xiaoqiang Li. Vision-language (VL) learning requires extensive visual perception capabilities, such as fine-grained object recognition and spatial perception. Recent works typically rely on training huge models on massive datasets to develop these capabilities. As a more efficient alternative, this paper proposes a new framework that T ransfers the knowledge from a hub o f V ision E xperts ( ToVE ) for efficient VL learning, leveraging pre-trained vision expert models to promote visual perception capability.

arxiv-2504-12951.title: Are Retrials All You Need? Enhancing Large Language Model Reasoning Without Verbalized Feedback
arxiv-2504-12951.creator: Nearchos Potamitis, Akhil Arora
arxiv-2504-12951.description: Abstract Recent advancements in large language models (LLMs) have catalyzed the development of general-purpose autonomous agents, demonstrating remarkable performance in complex reasoning tasks across various domains. This surge has spurred the evolution of a plethora of prompt-based reasoning frameworks. A recent focus has been on iterative reasoning strategies that refine outputs through self-evaluation and verbalized feedback.

arxiv-2512-00434.title: Privacy-Preserving Generative Modeling and Clinical Validation of Longitudinal Health Records for Chronic Disease
arxiv-2512-00434.creator: Benjamin D. Ballyk 1,2, Ankit Gupta 1, Sujay Konda 1, Kavitha Subramanian 4, Chris Landon 5, Ahmed Ammar Naseer 1, Georg Maierhofer 2,3, Sumanth Swaminathan 1,2, Vasudevan Venkateshwaran 1
arxiv-2512-00434.description: Abstract Data privacy is a critical challenge in modern medical workflows as the adoption of electronic patient records has grown rapidly. Stringent data protection regulations limit access to clinical records for training and integrating machine learning models that have shown promise in improving diagnostic accuracy and personalized care outcomes.

arxiv-2512-04759.title: Challenging the Abilities of Large Language Models in Italian: a Community Initiative
arxiv-2512-04759.creator: Malvina Nissim 22, Danilo Croce 27, Viviana Patti 31, Pierpaolo Basile 18, Giuseppe Attanasio 11, Elio Musacchio 18,26, Matteo Rinaldi 31, Federico Borazio 27, Maria Francis 22,30, Jacopo Gili 31, Daniel Scalena 22,23, Begoña Altuna 29, Ekhi Azurmendi 29, Valerio Basile 31, Luisa Bentivogli 6, Arian
arxiv-2512-04759.description: Abstract The rapid progress of Large Language Models (LLMs) has transformed natural language processing and broadened its impact across research and society. Yet, systematic evaluation of these models, especially for languages beyond English, remains limited. "Challenging the Abilities of LAnguage Models in ITAlian" (CALAMITA) is a large-scale collaborative benchmarking initiative for Italian, coordinated under the Italian Association for Computational Linguistics.

arxiv-2602-24043.title: Spatio-Temporal Garment Reconstruction Using Diffusion Mapping via Pattern Coordinates
arxiv-2602-24043.creator: Yingxuan You, Ren Li, Corentin Dumery, Cong Cao, Hao Li, Pascal Fua
arxiv-2602-24043.description: Abstract Reconstructing 3D clothed humans from monocular images and videos is a fundamental problem with applications in virtual try-on, avatar creation, and mixed reality. Despite significant progress in human body recovery, accurately reconstructing garment geometry, particularly for loose-fitting clothing, remains an open challenge. We propose a unified framework for high-fidelity 3D garment reconstruction from both single images and video sequences.

britannica-1911-linton-eliza-lynn.title: Linton, Eliza Lynn (1911 Encyclopaedia Britannica article)
britannica-1911-linton-eliza-lynn.creator: Encyclopaedia Britannica
britannica-1911-linton-eliza-lynn.description: Article 'Linton, Eliza Lynn' from the 1911 Encyclopædia Britannica (Volume 16), the classic English-language general encyclopedia, now in the public domain. Lynn, vicar of Crosthwaite, in Cumberland, was born at Keswick on the 10th of February 1822. She early manifested great independence of character, and in great measure educated herself from the stores of her father’s library.

pmc-10575187.title: An Improved Genetic Algorithm for the Recovery System of USVs Based on Stern Ramp Considering the Influence of Currents
pmc-10575187.creator: Lulu Zhou, Xiaoming Ye, Zehao Huang, Pengzhan Xie, Zhenguo Song, Yanjia Tong, Enrico Meli
pmc-10575187.description: With the progression of marine exploration and exploitation, as well as the advancements in mechanical intelligence, the utilization of the unmanned surface vehicle (USV) and the design of their guidance system have become prominent areas of focus. However, the stern ramp recovery of the USV is still in its infancy due to its unique attitude requirements and automation design.

pmc-12661365.title: Baseline Cytomegalovirus Immunoglobulin G Levels Predict Reactivation in Patients With Multiple Myeloma Receiving Elranatamab
pmc-12661365.creator: Ukyo Kondo, Taku Kikuchi, Shotaro Sugita, Miyu Watanabe, Chiaki Matsumoto, Moe Nomura‐Yogo, Kodai Kunisada, Kota Sato, Tomomi Takei, Mizuki Ogura, Yu Abe, Osamu Hosoya, Tadao Ishida, Nobuhiro Tsukada
pmc-12661365.description: BackgroundThe cumulative incidence and risk of cytomegalovirus (CMV) reactivation in patients with relapsed/refractory multiple myeloma (RRMM) receiving elranatamab remain unclear.MethodsWe retrospectively analyzed RRMM patients treated with elranatamab to assess cumulative incidence and risk factors for CMV reactivation.ResultsAmong 32 patients, the 6‐month cumulative incidence of CMV reactivation was 37.3%.

pmc-13330053.title: Latent transition analysis of end-of-life care trajectories among cancer patients in South Korea: a nationwide cohort study
pmc-13330053.creator: Goun Park, Wankyo Chung
pmc-13330053.description: BackgroundDespite the prolonged and often fragmented course of care before death among patients with cancer, end-of-life care research has largely relied on cross-sectional snapshots rather than the longitudinal trajectories needed to inform quality improvement. This study aimed to identify distinct end-of-life care trajectories among Korean cancer decedents.

pmc-13426925.title: It would be really great if I had greater confidence and ability there: Understanding the primary care physician experience with nutrition in training, clinical practice, and interprofessional collaboration
pmc-13426925.creator: Caitlin A. Hildebrand, Seema Agrawal, Jaclyn Albin, Gary L. Beck Dallaghan, Elizabeth Chen, David Gaviria, Kurt O. Gilliland, Alison Hilton, Thomas C. Keyserling, Elizabeth Mayer-Davis, Alice S. Ammerman
pmc-13426925.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). BackgroundPrimary care physicians (PCPs) are on the front lines of health promotion and disease prevention, yet evidence supports a longstanding gap in physicians’ capacity to counsel about diet, a key factor in patient health and chronic disease risk. Momentum to address the nutrition training needs of physicians is growing; however, challenges PCPs experience due to inadequate training are further complicated by clinical practice barriers.

pmc-13440198.title: Association of BCAAs/BCKAs with pancreatic steatosis in patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus: A cross‐sectional study
pmc-13440198.creator: Jie Gao, Pijun Cheng, Fusong Jiang, Wenmin Li, Yingying Shi, Wenjun Wang, Liang Wang, Tao Lei, Yunxiang Zang, Jun Lu
pmc-13440198.description: AimsTo examine the association between branched‐chain α‐keto acids (BCKAs) and pancreatic steatosis in patients with type 2 diabetes (T2DM).MethodsThis cross‐sectional study was conducted from January 2023 to March 2025. Upper abdominal computerized tomography was performed, pancreatic volume (PV), PV index (PVI), CT attenuation of pancreas (CTAP), and CTAp/s were then calculated.

pmc-13552972.title: Incidence and Risk Factors of Helicobacter pylori Infections Among Asymptomatic Pakistani Tobacco Consumers
pmc-13552972.creator: Rabia Zulfiqar, Saima Bukhari, Shovit Dutta, Imran Mahfooz Khan, Tariq Hassan, Jestoni Maniago
pmc-13552972.description: Objective:This study aimed to assess the incidence of H. pylori infection and its associated risk factors among asymptomatic Pakistani tobacco users, with the goal of informing targeted screening and prevention strategies.Methods:A cross-sectional study was conducted from September 2024 to February 2025 in Punjab and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan.
